name: Palifermin

lead: Palifermin (Kepivance) is a truncated recombinant human keratinocyte growth factor (KGF) given intravenously. It is approved to reduce the incidence and duration of severe oral mucositis in patients with blood cancers receiving high-dose chemotherapy with stem cell support.

It binds the KGF receptor on epithelial cells, which is reported to boost their growth, maturation and migration. Because the US label notes the receptor is present in skin, hair follicles and sebaceous glands, it is occasionally mentioned in skin-renewal discussions. The evidence is for mucositis; no cosmetic studies were found.

paras: It is given by intravenous infusion in hospital cancer care. It is used as supportive treatment, not as a cosmetic.
The label lists rash, fever, raised amylase, itching and swelling as common, and flags uncertain effects on tumors expressing KGF receptors and possible fetal harm. It is prescription-only.

angle.text: Palifermin is a prescription keratinocyte growth factor that stimulates epithelial cell growth, and it is occasionally mentioned in skin-renewal discussions. It is approved for chemotherapy mouth sores, which is where the evidence lies.

lead: Palifermin (brand name Kepivance) is a truncated recombinant human keratinocyte growth factor (KGF), a member of the fibroblast growth factor family produced in E. coli. It is approved to reduce the incidence and duration of severe oral mucositis in patients with blood cancers receiving high-dose chemotherapy with stem cell support [1].

It is a cancer supportive-care drug, not a cosmetic. It appears in appearance contexts only as a keratinocyte growth factor; the US label notes the KGF receptor is present in skin, hair follicles and sebaceous glands, but no studies for cosmetic use were found [1].
infobox: Severe oral mucositis in hematologic malignancy

paras: The US label indicates palifermin to decrease severe oral mucositis in patients with hematologic malignancies receiving myelotoxic therapy with autologous stem cell support, and states that safety and efficacy have not been established in non-hematologic malignancies [1]. Guidelines on mucositis and chemotherapy protectants discuss it as the first active drug approved for the condition [2][3].

In a double-blind trial of 212 patients with hematologic cancers receiving intensive therapy, palifermin was compared with placebo for oral mucositis [4]. Randomized placebo-controlled trials in head and neck cancer chemoradiotherapy also reported reduced severe mucositis [5][6]. Other registered trials examined it in stem cell transplantation, HIV, toxic epidermal necrolysis and multiple sclerosis [7][8][9]. Several were terminated or withdrawn.

The label lists rash, fever, elevated amylase, pruritus, erythema and edema as the most common reactions, and warns of a potential for stimulation of growth of KGF-receptor-expressing non-hematopoietic tumors. Animal studies showed embryo-fetal harm [1].
Palifermin binds the KGF receptor, reported to promote proliferation, differentiation and migration of epithelial cells [1].
